description: This map displays an urban and peri-urban area in Stockholm, Sweden, using false-colour infrared (FCIR) satellite or aerial imagery. In this imagery, healthy vegetation appears in red tones, built-up areas and impervious surfaces are shown in grey or bluish hues, and water bodies are dark blue to black. Overlaid on this base imagery are several vector features: light blue lines delineate the road network and its associated land, while thin yellow and green outlines define other land cover/land use (LULC) polygons. Visible geographic features include a major river or water body, dense urban development, industrial zones, extensive vegetated areas, an airport runway in the bottom-left, and a stadium or athletic track in the bottom-middle. The map serves as an example for the classification of "Road network and its associated land" for Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) guidelines, highlighting features with a minimum mapping width of 10 metres. The credit for the image is K. Larsson.
